A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenLIP work. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and matching equations, tables and relocated figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal benchmark evaluations, scaling experiments, ablations, discriminative transfer results and qualitative generations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds benchmark evaluations, controlled initialization and register-token comparisons, and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed GenLIP architecture, prefix-LM attention, MRoPE, autoregressive objective, gated attention and vision-feature extraction remain unchanged. Describing the gate as per-head adds implementation specificity without establishing a procedural change. The new SAIL and register-token variants are experimental comparisons.

E1.justification: The Cambrian-style evaluation adds knowledge, mathematical reasoning and perception coverage through MMMU, MathVista, MMVP, SEED-Image and CV-Bench2D/3D (v2 Tables 5 and 12). MMBench and RealWorldQA already appeared in v1's unfrozen evaluation. The unmapped Dataset-S1/S2 labels do not establish whether training-data coverage actually changed.

E2.justification: v1 discusses SAIL without experimentally comparing it. v2 Table 9 evaluates SAIL-style Qwen3-0.6B models with initialization and gating variants, while Table 10 adds one-register and four-register alternatives against gated attention. The comparator sets in the retained main evaluations are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include projector-only versus projector-plus-LLM perplexity evaluation, matched 1B-sample initialization/register experiments, and attention-map analysis using 128×128 images, six prompt tokens and 30 generated tokens. Appendix aggregation is corrected from 15 to 14 benchmarks, matching the already stated main-text suite; this does not establish rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds objective-mismatch diagnostics, controlled tests of pretrained language initialization, and comparisons of gating against register tokens. Expanded Figure 3 and new Figures 10–11 investigate attention allocation and language-side sinks. Existing scaling, resolution-sensitivity and qualitative failure analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new layer-averaged attention curves are descriptive measurements, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark and ablation results. Table 9 reports 56.0 for scratch-trained SAIL-g versus 54.8 with initialization; Table 10 reports 56.3 for gating versus 55.1 with four registers. Table 8 adds captioning results and replaces subgroup averages with an overall average. Figure 3 replaces the earlier single attention curve with separate measurements. Retained headline tables are unchanged; the additions do not establish same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The sequence definition, autoregressive loss and gating equations (1–3) are unchanged. The added language-prior discussion provides empirical interpretation, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a simple, scalable generative vision encoder with competitive performance and strong data efficiency. The revised abstract explicitly states 8B versus SigLIP2's 40B seen samples, quantifying an existing claim. The new diagnostics support the retained alignment rationale rather than redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.4.2 and new Appendix E argue that pretrained language initialization can encourage language-side shortcuts and weaken visual grounding, whereas training from scratch promotes attention to visual evidence. This adds a substantive mechanism hypothesis and qualification on initialization benefits. v2 also softens the claim that ungated models 'fail' at discriminative tasks to substantially degraded performance; the existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 identifies Recap-DataComp-1B and the 27M BLIP3o-Long-Caption/10M Infinity-MM mixture. v2 replaces this provenance with unmapped Dataset-S1/S2 labels in Section 3.3 and Table 1. Conversely, it adds exact frozen-evaluation resolutions, per-head gating specificity and implementation details for new comparisons. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish an actual training-data replacement.

R1.justification: v2 extends the existing distinction from SAIL with an argument about initialization, adds benchmark citations and attention-sink alternatives such as DINOv3 and Systematic Outliers, and removes four training-data-related references. The broader positioning among contrastive, encoder-decoder and single-transformer approaches is retained.

P1.justification: The qualitative 'Let ViT Speak' section moves from Section 4.1 to 4.6, allowing setup and quantitative results to lead the experiments. Appendix sections are reorganized, and terminology, grammar, captions, conclusion wording and an author affiliation are edited. Most existing prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 9, 10 and 12, appends a perplexity panel to Figure 1, expands Figure 3 into three panels, and introduces attention plots and heatmaps in Figures 10–11. The controlled VLP table gains captioning columns and changes its averages. Existing qualitative and scaling figures are relocated, while several tables receive revised layouts.

improvement.justification: The SAIL/register comparisons, broader benchmark coverage and attention analyses strengthen empirical support for important design choices. However, removing identifiable training datasets and mixture provenance materially weakens reproducibility and leaves continuity of the training data unresolved. The PDFs provide no mapping for Dataset-S1/S2, so the gains and this substantial reporting loss do not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
